definitions.explanation: Neither fully done nor properly abandoned — stuck in an unsatisfying middle state. Describes work, effort, attitudes, or situations that lack commitment or completion.

examples.japanese: {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}な{気持|きも}ちではだめだ。
{仕事|しごと}を{中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}に{残|のこ}したまま{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: I left work with things half-finished.

examples.japanese: {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}な{知識|ちしき}で{人|ひと}にアドバイスするのは{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: Giving people advice with incomplete knowledge is dangerous.

notes:
{中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ} conveys a strong sense of dissatisfaction with something incomplete or uncommitted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}な{気持|きも}ち (half-hearted feelings)
- {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}な{知識|ちしき} (incomplete knowledge)
- {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}に{終|お}わる (end inconclusively)
- {中途半端|ちゅうとはんぱ}にする (leave half-done)

This word carries a negative nuance — it implies that something should have been done fully or not at all. It is commonly used to criticize lack of commitment or thoroughness.
